body:
I'd change `access the translation server` to `access the main translation domain`. It's still okay to access regular methods like `compare_locales()` and `get_locale_name()`. Only methods acting as proxies for the main translation domain may pose risks.

Also, there are `tool scripts`, `[code]@tool[/code] scripts` and `[code]tool[/code] scripts` in the repository. I guess it's better to use `tool scripts` as it's the general concept, whereas the latter two are GDScript-specific.

As for the last sentence suggesting the creation of custom domains, I don't think it's a silver bullet that will fulfill most needs. It's kind of similar to adding "Create a custom LineEdit instead" in the warning about accessing the internal `LineEdit` of  `SpinBox`:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/88b9932ce14412843538b5084d3563ed89dbb308/doc/classes/SpinBox.xml#L40-L45

body:
I was deliberately trying to simplify. Provide the general advice for the less versed users and mention enough detail to the power users to let them figure out why the advise breaks and where it is applicable.

But to make it easier to understand, I would maybe just change the order in witch information is being provided.

```suggestion
		[b]Note:[/b] When using translations in [code]tool scripts[/code], it is recommended to access a custom domain using [method get_or_add_domain] instead of [TranslationServer]. This avoids using the main domain while it is intended to be in control of the editor.
```
My rationale:
WHEN translating in tool scripts (*while you would use the main domain*), it is recommended to access a custom domain instead of [TranslationServer] (*you can use that domain like you would use TranslationServer for translations*). This avoids the main domain in control of the editor. (*here's the reason you see odd behaviour*)

@timothyqiu wrote
> I don't think it's a silver bullet that will fulfill most needs

Yeah but I think it may prevent a lot of the weird and difficult to debug issues from arising? Hm, maybe this could also be a good wording.

```suggestion
		[b]Note:[/b] Some unexpected behavior of translations in [code]tool scripts[/code] can be avoided accessing a custom domain instead of [TranslationServer] directly. This avoids using the main domain while it is intended to be in control of the editor.
```

This would put emphasis of this not being a silver bullet...
